title: What does the middle one get?
hook: Two people split $1 evenly. Add a third who can only deal with one of them. Now what?

doesNotKnow: that the person with a spare partner can push the split almost all the way to themselves

misconception: Two people bargaining over $1 split it about evenly, whoever else is around.
objective: The learner can explain that on a line of three, whichever end the centre leaves out will offer to take less, so the ends bid each other down until the centre has the whole $1 (in the limit), the only stable split.

claims.text: On the stage, each round the end Bo left out offers to take 10 cents less and Bo switches, so Bo's share goes $0.50, $0.60, $0.70, $0.80, $0.90, $1.00 (the round-by-round trace), the asks fall from $0.50 to $0.00, and Bo gets the whole $1.
claims.source: Lesson rule (10-cent undercut). Demo.tsx round(k): Bo's share 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0; re-run in node (ncm-e00). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node: rounds 0..5 matched ask 50,40,30,20,10,0 cents, Bo 50..100; LAST = 50/10 = 5 rounds; stage message "No one can ask less than $0. Stable." at round 5. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v2, wave E r6 revision by demo-builder): reveal now quotes the on-stage round-by-round trace of Bo's share. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own run of round(k): Bo 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100 cents; partner ask 50, 40, 30, 20, 10, 0, each 10 below the previous partner's; reveal trace and 'asks fell from $0.50 to $0.00' match. Trace kept through '2 people'.

claims.text: On a line of three where the centre can deal with only one end, the only stable outcome (no one can undercut, and no pair could both do better by dealing together) gives the centre the whole $1, in the limit; the centre's power comes from the spare partner, not from bargaining skill.
claims.source: An unmatched end gets 0, so it would accept any positive share; the matched end's share must be 0 or the left-out end can offer Bo more. Brief check: {centre: 1, endMatched: 0}. Easley and Kleinberg 2010, ch. 12 (stability). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own derivation (E&K stability: no unmatched pair with x_u + x_v < 1): the unmatched end gets 0, so the centre must have x_B >= 1, hence B = 1 and the matched end 0; the empty matching is unstable. Unique up to which end is matched. E&K ch. 12 (Bargaining and Power in Networks) placement agrees with my knowledge; book not opened.

claims.text: In this model two people with no one else to turn to split the $1 evenly.
claims.source: Lesson rule (symmetric split with equal, zero outside options). Stage message 'No one else to turn to: they split evenly.' | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Convention, on stage: 2-person message "No one else to turn to: they split evenly."; Bo 50.

claims.text: The lesson is a simplified model: one deal per person, 10-cent undercuts, two people alone split evenly.
claims.source: Assumptions of Demo.tsx; stage chip 'Model: each person makes one deal' and the reveal's last line. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Convention, on stage: chip "Model: each person makes one deal"; reveal muted line lists the three rules.

recall.question: Dee can split $1 with Eli or with Fay, but only one of them; Eli and Fay have no one else. In a stable outcome, what does Dee get?
recall.why: Whoever Dee leaves out gets nothing, so they offer to take less; the two bid each other down until Dee has (nearly) the whole $1.
